title: Sort by Several Keys with Tuples
hints: Tuples of comparable values compare element by element, left to right.
Build a tuple of sort keys per row; negate numbers you want sorted descending.
jsBridge: JS sort comparators return numbers (`b.points - a.points || ...`). Swift's `sorted(by:)` takes a **Bool** "are these in increasing order" predicate, and tuples of `Comparable`s compare lexicographically: `(-p1, -w1, n1) < (-p2, -w2, n2)`.

compass.q: JS comparators return -1/0/1. Swift's return `Bool`. Why is a Bool predicate enough, and what rule must it obey (strict weak ordering)?
Tuple comparison vs `[SortDescriptor]` vs `KeyPathComparator`: which scales to user-selectable sort columns?
Tuple comparison works up to 6 elements. Why is there a limit? Does parameter packs change it?
Is Swift's `sort` stable? Does it matter when users sort a list by one column after another?
